boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen White Oak Road record (March 31, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. Dinwiddie Court House (VA086) is the same day. Humphreys commanded the Second Corps, and his account of its actions here is a participant's. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Corps' and the live field zero. Humphreys names Ayres's, Crawford's and Griffin's divisions of the Fifth Corps and Miles's division of the Second against McGowan's, Gracie's (Sanford's), Hunton's and Wise's brigades, and quotes Ayres that Winthrop turned back on seeing a much superior force; Johnson says his line was McGowan's, Moody's (Stansel's) and Hunton's brigades, with Wise's moved out on the left by Lee's order.
claims.rationale: Formation lists and one attributed impression; no headcount for either side on March 31. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Humphreys places Ayres in open ground south of the road, says a branch of Gravelly Run had become swollen and hard to cross, and describes the Confederate works on the crest of a long slope with wide slashings, abatis and artillery, 'unused and in good order', whose slashing stopped Hays at the Crow house; Johnson says the Union line re-formed on vantage ground west of a branch of Gravelly Run.
claims.rationale: The works and slashings predate the day; the swollen stream follows the night's rain, and the rifle-pits Johnson later held were thrown up by Union skirmishers the night before. Mixed; not tagged inherited as a whole. No map verification.

claims.value: Humphreys says Lee was on the ground directing the movement, relays Hunton that he had no orders to attack and McGowan that he ordered the charge when the firing began, and says he himself ordered Miles to attack the Confederate left flank; Johnson says he ordered his command forward to meet the Union attack, and that Anderson later ordered it withdrawn. NPS credits the counterattack to Johnson. The frozen commanders are Lee and Anderson (CS) and Warren (US); the live page lists Warren and 'Major General Robert Lee'.
claims.rationale: Accounts of who started the Confederate attack differ and are attributed, not reconciled; Humphreys' order to Miles is his own participant account. Anderson's own direction is described only in Johnson's report; the live rank is not adopted. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 2,670 (US 1,870; CS 800) and the live field 3,016 (US 1,781; CS 1,235). Humphreys gives Warren's 936 killed and wounded and 470 missing (1,406), 374 killed and wounded in the Second Corps and more than 300 prisoners taken by Miles; Johnson gives the enemy's loss as including about 470 prisoners and his own as about 800, and the note after his report gives 187 for the White Oak road.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Johnson's 800 equals the frozen Confederate figure and his 470 prisoners Warren's 470 missing; these are observations, not established sources for either figure.

open_questions: Warren's, Ayres's, Crawford's and Griffin's reports (Nos. 74, 91, 97, 77), Humphreys' own report (No. 21), Miles's report (selected; cited under VA090 and VA094, not used here under the ceiling), McGowan's, Hunton's and Wise's accounts, Wallace's report (No. 274), the Warren Court of Inquiry record and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
